model_interpretation.claim: Each accepted light contribution builds a normalized half-vector component by component, then uses only its dot product with the surface normal. Computing dot(N,H) and multiplying by the same reciprocal half-vector length is algebraically equivalent and avoids scaling all three components. The prior light-packing candidate was valid and measured faster than baseline, but the catalog has only one distinct T3 program; this contrasting change isolates BRDF arithmetic. Floating-point ordering changes slightly, so the controller must verify the one-level tolerance across its checks, including altered light colors.

model_interpretation.claim: For each contributing light, the current code normalizes L=d/r and then normalizes L−V. Since r>0, L−V and d−rV have the same direction; compute N·L as dot(N,d)/r and N·H as dot(N,d−rV)/|d−rV| instead. This removes component-wise normalization of both vectors while preserving the BRDF algebraically; the reordered floating-point operations require controller validation. The catalog reports three distinct valid programs (no repeats): baseline 0.11495 s, direct half-vector dot 0.10920 s, packed-light cache 0.11101 s, and their measured combination 0.10518 s. This contrasts with the cache and previous half-vector formulations by testing a scale-invariant half-vector representation, not by assuming an unmeasured gain.

items.subject: Optimize per-pixel shading math and row-wise vectorization
items.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, focus on ShadeTileC's per-pixel BRDF evaluation: investigate safe reuse of pixel and light values, reducing expensive normalization/pow work, and/or row-wise compiler vectorization. Preserve the original shading semantics closely; any approximation must meet the one-intensity-level tolerance on all correctness checks, including altered light colors, and must not rely on a single expected frame. Do not change the tile-culling strategy or introduce threading in this branch; measure both 1- and 4-core cases and retain a portable path unless the frozen build proves a specific ISA is available.
